clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 8041 is its operative paragraph, which exempts Henry Clarke Hill from compulsory retirement for age "for a period not in excess of one year from March 1, 1939". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires exempting Henry Clarke Hill, who, during the month of February, 1939, "will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service". The command is a time-limited permission for one named employee, so it ended by its own terms: the period is capped at one year from March 1, 1939, so the latest day it could run is February 29, 1940 (1940 was a leap year), recorded inclusive; the alternative anniversary reading would end it on March 1, 1940. The wording "not in excess of" states a ceiling rather than a fixed length, and the order itself fixes no shorter period; no held source shows any act that shortened it, and the later order EO 8328 starts its further exemption on March 1, 1940, consistent with the first period having run through February 29, 1940. EO 8328 (dated January 22, 1940 in its text) recites this order by number and further exempts the same employee "for a period not in excess of six months from March 1, 1940"; it is recorded as a later event (a separate later exemption, an extension), not as the end of this order's command, which ended by its own stated period.

research_rationale:
EO 8041 (January 25, 1939) exempts Henry Clarke Hill from compulsory retirement for age "for a period not in excess of one year from March 1, 1939", under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404). I read the registered American Presidency Project transcription in full, confirmed its identity against the Common Crawl capture record (number, date, subject heading and text hash agree), and confirmed that it contains one operative command. The clause ended by its own stated period on February 29, 1940, recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading disclosed. Later extension orders are recorded as later events and do not end this order's clause. The text is a transcription (grade mirror_transcription) and the original is not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.

savings.reason: The order grants one named employee a permission to remain in service despite the retirement-age rule for a stated period and contains no savings, transition or continuing-obligation clause. Service the employee performed while the exemption was in force is a completed effect that does not depend on the order remaining in force, and no held source shows any other residual effect; it is recorded as accrued.
